Commentary.Commentary: We are back with Australia's reply with the bat! The Indian team can be seen in a huddle with skipper Bumrah giving a pep-talk to his men. The Australian opening pair of Sam Konstas and Usman Khawaja walk out to the crease as the Indians scatter to take their fielding positions. Jasprit Bumrah has the new ball and is all in readiness with three slips in position. Off we go...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

Well then, after a tidy and disciplined bowling performance, the Aussies will aim to replicate the same with the bat. However, it will be a challenge in itself to face Jasprit Bumah and Co. with the new ball, on a surface that has been really tough to bat on. Australia's aim will be to go unscathed in this phase of play while a wicket or two might help India to gain some early control. Stick around with us as Australia's response with the bat is just a few moments away.

With all the recognized batters in the sheds, Washington Sundar offered some resistance but he too, couldn't last long in the middle either. A few punches from the lower order, including those vital boundaries by Bumrah propelled India to go past 180. The Australian bowling attack performed in unison as Boland and Starc were the chief destructors, while Cummins snagged a couple, and Lyon with a solitary wicket. None of the Indian batters could complete his fifty,and  though there were starts for several batters, they couldn't get going and lost their wickets at regular intervals. Pant was the highest scorer with 40-odd runs and that was it.

Post Lunch, Scott Boland struck again, enticing Kohli to edge one outside off. Rishabh Pant and Ravindra Jadeja then got together and offered stubborn resistance against a disciplined Aussie attack. Their partnership showed glimpses of stability, though runs came at a premium. Pant curbed his customary approach and adapted to the conditions, limiting to just block and leave for a fair bit, but Boland returned to deliver a decisive blow as he got rid of Pant and Reddy off successive balls. Jadeja who was dropped on the scores of 3 and 5 by Smith and Lyon respectively, perished eventually as well, leaving India reeling at 134/7 down.

A job well done by Australia with the ball, to say the least. And an equally disappointing performance with the bat from the Indians that can be seen over a sorry-looking batting card. After losing the toss on a greenish surface under overcast skies, Australia made the most of the conditions with relentless pressure from both ends. The openers fell early, leaving India in trouble before Virat Kohli and Shubman Gill steadied the ship with a crucial partnership. However, a lapse in concentration saw Gill dismissed on the last ball before Lunch.

Pat Cummins continued to shuffle his bowlers masterfully, ensuring they stayed fresh and ready to apply pressure. The Australian bowlers responded well, maintaining discipline and consistently probing away at the Indian batters. Despite the constant challenges, Pant and Jadeja held firm. Pant, in particular, started to find some rhythm towards the end of the session, picking up a couple of boundaries. The question now is whether he will continue to curb his natural attacking instincts, as he did for the majority of the second session, or if he will shift gears and counterpunch as the innings progresses. Either way, it promises to be an intriguing continuation with the third session scheduled to commence at 10 am IST (4.30 am GMT). Cheers!

SESSION SUMMARY - 25 overs, 50 runs, and 1 wicket. End of a gritty session of Test cricket! The session run rate of 2 clearly reflects the pressure the Aussie bowlers exerted in the afternoon session, making scoring difficult for the Indians. That's Lunch on Day 1 at the SCG, and what a first session it's been! The Aussie bowlers have been right on the money, asking questions, and have created chances constantly, keeping the Indian batters on their toes. Looking ahead, conditions should ease up for batting as the day wears on. Kohli will be joined by a new batter at the crease and India will have to rebuild once again from scratch. Australia's aim would be to prevent the partnerships from settling in. We've got a fascinating post-Lunch session coming up at 7.40 am IST (2.10 am GMT). Stick around!

Cummins kept the bowling changes coming, making the most of a pitch that had the ball dancing around. India's scoring rate crawled along as the batters battled both bounce and movement. After that early scare, Kohli seemed to have got his nerves settled and played the ball inside the line and closer to the body. However, both the batters did well enough to neutralize any further casualties before that brain fade moment as Gill ran out of patience and nicked it to the slips on the stroke of Lunch.

The introduction of Scott Boland proved to be a good one as he made immediate inroads, sending Jaiswal packing in the very first over. And all of a sudden, both openers were back in the pavilion within the first hour of play. Boland nearly added Kohli to his tally, targeting the right-hander's well-documented weakness outside off-stump, but fortune smiled on the batter as he survived the testing spell.

Overcast skies, grassy pitch with a fair bit of movement either way. A bowler's treat to start with as Australia were invited to bowl first. The Indian openers did start off cautiously with Jaiswal being watchful and KL Rahul not poking at anything served outside off. Cummins and Starc examined both of them for a fair bit and set up a strong tone with the ball.  Starc drew first blood, inducing a breakthrough and dismissing Rahul that resulted in a soft dismissal.

LUNCH, DAY 1 - 25 overs, 57 runs and 3 wickets! Australia's session fair and square. The hosts have managed to send the top three of the opposition back into the sheds and are firmly in the driver's seat at the moment. India would be very disappointed as after two quick breakthroughs, things did settle up nicely for them as the Gill and Kohli alliance was blossoming at a gentle pace. However, Test cricket is all about sustainability and the ability to maintain the patience level, where Gill miserably threw away his wicket.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! Nathan Lyon strikes at the stroke of the Lunch break! Something seemed to be brewing as the men around the bat exchanged a few words with Gill, who wandered down the track before this ball to ensure it was the last over before the break. This is pushed across the right-hander by Lyon, on a nagging length, around off, Gill premeditates as he charges down the track. He is nowhere near the pitch of the ball and just hangs his bat out there to defend. The outside edge is found and it goes straight to Steven Smith at first slip who takes it near his waist safely. Gill is absolutely distraught. Australia's happiness knows no bounds as they get around Lyon. THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 1!

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the national anthems and it's now time to set the ball rolling in Sydney. Adam Gilchrist informs us that the first three days of the Test have been sold out. Pat Cummins and Co. are in a huddle before taking their respective positions in the field. KL Rahul is back at the top of the order alongside Yashasvi Jaiswal. Mitchell Starc has the new ball in hand and he is raring to go. Three slips and a gully await. The wait is over. Here we go!

Before we get underway, it's time for the pre-match formalities. Ravi Shastri and Mark Taylor bring the trophy out and place it on the pedestal. Pat Cummins and Jasprit Bumrah lead their respective sides out for the national anthems. First up, it will be India's national anthem, followed by that of Australia.

PITCH REPORT - Sunil Gavaskar is pitchside. He says it is a very grassy pitch with 7mm of grass all over the deck. He also reckons that he hasn't seen so much grass on the first day of any of the last four Tests. Adds that batting won't be easy at all, especially with overhead conditions. He believes that the ball will seam and swing either way and the batters might have a hard time initially against the new ball.

Live visuals show Mark Waugh handing Beau Webster his maiden Test cap. The Tasmanian all-rounder, surrounded by friends and family, becomes the 469th player to represent Australia in Test cricket. Meanwhile, in the Indian camp, Virat Kohli is doing all the talking in the huddle.

The captain of Australia, Pat Cummins says that they would have batted first as well. Hopes to get the ball to swing around early under overcast conditions. Mentions that the last week in Melbourne was amazing and it is always a wonderful occasion here. Shares that every summer, the support for Test cricket keeps getting bigger, and it's truly heartening to see. Informs about the one change with Beau Webster making his Test debut, replacing Mitchell Marsh.

Jasprit Bumrah, the stand-in captain of India says that they have played some really good cricket and hopes to put up a good show. About the pitch, he says it doesn't look like it has many demons. Also says that there's a bit of grass covering and doesn't look very spicy either. Mentions they always need to digest the defeat and embrace the wins. Adds that the chat was to keep the spirits high. Informs there are two changes. On Rohit, he says that the skipper has shown great leadership always and that Rohit has opted to rest whereas, Akash Deep misses out due to injury and Shubman Gill and Prasidh Krishna are in the side.

India (Playing XI) - Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul, Shubman Gill (In for Rohit Sharma), Virat Kohli, Rishabh Pant (WK), Ravindra Jadeja, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar, Jasprit Bumrah (C), Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna (In for Akash Deep).

Australia (Playing XI) - Sam Konstas, Usman Khawaja, Marnus Labuschagne, Steven Smith, Travis Head, Beau Webster (On debut) (In for Mitchell Marsh), Alex Carey (WK), Pat Cummins (C), Mitchell Starc, Nathan Lyon, Scott Boland.
TOSS - India have won the toss and they will BAT first.

Right then, the suspense, or should we say a part of it, is over. Jasprit Bumrah has been spotted wearing the Indian blazer as he heads out for the toss. It’s confirmed that Bumrah will lead India in this Test. Also, it’s an overcast morning in Sydney, which could influence the decision at the toss.

The pre-match pressers have added to the intrigue, particularly regarding the Indian camp. When asked if Rohit Sharma would play in this Test, Indian head coach Gautam Gambhir stated they would decide after assessing the surface. Make of that what you will. On the injury front, Gambhir confirmed Akash Deep's unavailability due to a back issue. For Australia, Pat Cummins confirmed a debut for all-rounder Beau Webster, replacing Mitchell Marsh. It's all set up for an enthralling few days ahead. Stick around for the toss and team news!

As for India, they let the Aussies off the hook after having them at 91-6 in the second innings. Then, they crumbled in the final session as the hosts pounced on an opening. The tourists are now scrambling to reach their third consecutive WTC final, needing a win to stay in contention. Anything less than that would end their hopes.

Starting with Australia, they showed remarkable resilience at Melbourne, fighting back from tough situations to win a final-day thriller. The victory gave them a 2-1 series lead and boosted their World Test Championship final hopes. With this final Test against India and two more in Sri Lanka, Pat Cummins and his men need just one win to join South Africa in the summit clash.

Welcome to the iconic Sydney Cricket Ground, where the stage is set for the traditional New Year's Test, with the venue resplendent in its signature pink hue in support of the McGrath Foundation. Founded by former Aussie legend Glenn McGrath after the passing of his wife Jane McGrath to breast cancer, the foundation continues to make a difference in the fight against the disease.

Hello, everyone! We hope your New Year celebrations were everything you dreamed of, and if your resolutions have already taken a backseat, don’t fret - we are not here to judge! But enough of that, because it’s time for serious business as we gear up for the final chapter of the 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy.
